source.title: Synthesizing Physics Formulae with Transformers
claims_as_reported: roughly ten-second formula synthesis on selected SRBench/LLM-SRBench tasks
improved extrapolation on evaluated tasks at comparable inference-time budgets
weaker results on LSR-Synth at input scales far from training distribution
roughly two weeks of training on one H100 80 GB GPU for a roughly 145-million-parameter model
limitations: inference time is not full training-plus-inference lifecycle cost
benchmark formula accuracy is not proof of physical adequacy

lanes.A: Reusable formula-discovery comparison contract added; no quantum workload advantage.
lanes.B: No provider adapter or QPU job changed; simulator/dry-run-first policy unchanged.
lanes.C: Peak memory, token count and optional energy are explicit; no memory-replacement claim.
lanes.D: No device/process/packaging result; H100 requirement is an external model-training input.
lanes.E: No biomass, material, bio-oil or fusion result; future constitutive-model use remains hypothetical.
lanes.F: Owns evidence contract, reproducibility record, RG-046 and matched-budget gate.
lanes.G: Training resource provenance may feed future equipment/factory models; no fabrication result.
lanes.H: Dated publication connects model-training amortization to FIN-001/INV-033 and external infrastructure to INV-029.

evidence_boundary: All implementation fixtures are synthetic MODEL_ONLY tests. No generated equation is a physical law. No QPU, material, fuel, net-electricity, WACC or Data-Center-to-Phone claim is promoted.
next_gate: Pin the paper source/model/data versions, verify row-level split disjointness, run >=30 seeds per method at matched budgets, include training amortization and independent replication, then define a domain-specific discriminating experiment before any physical claim.
